steps.text:
Welcome, [b]General[/b]. The United Kingdom is yours.

Before we fight, learn to read the table. This will be brief.

First, the [b]map[/b]. Every country you can hold, supply and score is on it.

Pan with [b]W A S D[/b] or the arrow keys. Zoom with the [b]mouse wheel[/b].

Go on — look around. The war will wait.

Six [b]factions[/b] fight this war.

[b]Germany[/b], [b]Italy[/b] and [b]Japan[/b].
[b]The United Kingdom[/b], [b]the Soviet Union[/b] and [b]the United States[/b].

Each has its own hand, its own units and its own score.

Those six form two [b]teams[/b].

Germany, Italy and Japan are the [b]Axis[/b] — your side during this tutorial.
The UK, the Soviets and the US are the [b]Allies[/b].

You score for yourself, but you win as a team: the three factions' points are added together.

A [b]round[/b] is one turn for each faction, always in the same order:

[b]Germany[/b] → [b]UK[/b] → [b]Japan[/b] → [b]Soviet Union[/b] → [b]Italy[/b] → [b]United States[/b]

So you move first, and the enemy answers immediately.

Every turn runs the same seven steps, in order:

[b]1. Start[/b] — activate cards already in play
[b]2. Play Card[/b] — play one card from your hand
[b]3. Supply[/b] — units cut off from supply are removed
[b]4. Victory Points[/b] — score the supply stars you hold
[b]5. Discard[/b] — throw away any cards you do not want
[b]6. Draw[/b] — refill your hand back up to seven
[b]7. End[/b] — the turn passes to the next faction

[b]Play Card[/b] is the heart of it — one card, once, and the turn is spent.

[b]Discard[/b] and [b]Draw[/b] work as a pair: throw away what you cannot use, and the draw hands you fresh cards up to seven. A dead hand is your own fault, General.

The prompts will tell you when a step wants something from you.

But understand what you are spending.

That number is your [b]draw deck[/b], and it is finite. Nothing shuffles your discards back into it — when the deck is empty, it is empty, and the Draw step hands you nothing at all. A faction that has burned through its deck fights on with whatever is still in its hand.

And the enemy can burn it for you.

Some cards force you to discard straight off the top of your [b]draw deck[/b], sight unseen. Once that deck has run dry, every card you are ordered to discard and cannot costs you [b]one victory point[/b].

An empty deck does not just starve you, General. It bleeds you.

And the [b]goal[/b], General.

A war runs at most [b]20 rounds[/b]. Score more than the enemy team over those rounds and it is yours.

But it can end sooner.

The score is only judged at the [b]end of a round[/b] — after the [b]United States[/b] has finished its turn, the last of the six. Never in the middle.

If a team is [b]30 or more points ahead[/b] at that moment, the war stops there and then and that team has won. Otherwise the next round begins.

This lesson is a single round. Nobody wins today.

This is your [b]Play[/b] step — one card per turn, no more.

Play [b]Build Army[/b]. The rest of your hand is greyed out for now.

steps.note: Build Navy stays visible but unplayable, so the player can see what they are not doing yet.

steps.text:
Western Europe is holding a supply star. You can build an army there, and it will be supplied and score for you. 

 Select Western Europe to build an army.

Now you have an army in Western Europe. Congratulations! 

 Because Western Europe has a Supply Star, this will score you an extra 2 points during the Victory Point step, and it will be supplied during the Supply step. You are ready to move on.

Each faction can only have one army or navy in a country at a time. 

 You can not share a country with an enemy, but you can share it with an ally. A country holding two units will need to be battled twice to remove both units.

If ever you share a supply star with an ally, you will score only 1 point during your Victory Point step. 

 Your ally will also score 1 point during their Victory Point step. That is, if they still have an army there during their Victory Point step.
The [b]Victory Point[/b] step — step four. You score for every [b]supply star[/b] you occupy, and the fewer rivals standing on it, the more it pays.
Turn 2. The [b]United Kingdom[/b] answers — watch, you have nothing to do here.

That is a full round — every faction has taken a turn.

Well done, General. [b]Dismissed.[/b]
